text: A console print is only useful while someone's watching a terminal. This lesson writes every check's result into a real table in the warehouse instead, so a human can review it later, on their own schedule.

dw.DataQualityLog lives in the same schema as everything else in this capstone, which means finding every failed check in the last 30 days is just an ordinary WHERE clause — not a script that has to parse a text file by hand.

Windows Task Scheduler runs this exact script automatically, every night, a few minutes after the warehouse's own refresh job finishes — never before it, since checking yesterday's data and calling it done would defeat the whole purpose.

With this in place, the validation genuinely runs with zero humans involved on a normal night. Next chapter builds the first front-end on top of this now-validated warehouse: the Executive Power BI dashboard.
